(A) Goodwill represents a sum equal to the profits the purchaser is likely to receive from the running business during its first few years.
(B) The purchaser pays goodwill for profits expected only after the initial years of operation.
(C) The method assumes that a new business will earn profits during its first few years.
(D) Under the method, past average profits have no bearing on goodwill.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: ["(A) only","(B) and (C) only","(A) and (D) only","(B), (C) and (D) only"]
explanation: The method’s rationale links goodwill paid for a running business to the profits the purchaser is likely to receive in its first few years, while assuming a new business will not earn profits during that period. Thus, statement (A) is correct. Past average profits are used to calculate goodwill under this method, so statement (D) is incorrect.
